content:
The brand new iPhone 18 Pro's battery life has been significantly improved compared to previous models, and wired charging speeds have also been further accelerated.

Apple says that to fast-charge the new iPhone, you need to pair it with its 40W Dynamic Power Adapter (with a maximum output of 60W) and a USB-C cable. With this combination, charging speed can reach its limit, about 33% faster than previous Pro iPhones.

With a 60W charger, the iPhone 18 Pro can go from zero battery to 50% in about 15 minutes. By comparison, that's roughly 5 minutes faster than the iPhone 17 Pro.

In addition, with this faster charging speed, Apple says that just 5 minutes of charging can give users about 6 hours of video playback time.

Specifically, Apple lists the iPhone 18's fast-charging specs as requiring a 60W power adapter that supports Adjustable Voltage Supply functionality and meets the USB PD 3.1 standard. Currently, the only readily available charger on the market that meets these requirements is Apple's 40W Dynamic Power Adapter.

Once we actually get the phone in hand, we'll run real-world battery charging tests with other third-party adapters to see how it performs. For example, the MacBook charger you already have at home is usually 96W or 140W, but it lacks Adjustable Voltage Supply functionality.

There are also a ton of third-party chargers over 40W available, like this Anker 45W compact charger. The iPhone 18 Pro is expected to perform similarly to the iPhone 17 Pro, taking roughly 20 minutes to charge from zero to 50%. If you're rushing out the door, that's actually a pretty fast charging speed.

On the wireless charging front, the iPhone 18 Pro paired with an Apple MagSafe charger and any 35W power adapter can charge from 0% to 50% in about 30 minutes.

iPhone 18 Pro pre-orders start this Saturday, with the first batch shipping on September 18. Apple's foldable iPhone Duo, when it launches next month, will also support the same faster charging speeds as the iPhone 18 Pro as long as it's equipped with the appropriate accessories mentioned above.

Keep in mind that Apple no longer includes a charger in the box—just a USB-C cable.
